classification.difficultyReason: Chooses ten additional players with the captain compulsory, then orders all eleven while recognising that inclusion fixes no batting position.

content.prompt: A cricket club has one designated captain and 14 other members. A team of 11 is to be chosen for a match, and the batting order (positions 1 through 11) fixed. The captain must be included in the team. How many distinct batting orders are possible?

answer.short:
$\binom{14}{10}11!=39\,956\,716\,800$ batting orders.

Choose the other ten players, then arrange all eleven; the captain has no specified batting position.
answer.worked:
With the captain included, choose ten of the other fourteen members in $\binom{14}{10}$ ways. Arrange the eleven selected players in $11!$ ways.

$$\begin{align*}N&=\binom{14}{10}11!\\N&=1001\times39\,916\,800\\N&=39\,956\,716\,800\end{align*}$$
